Raymond III was born around 1140 to Raymond II Count of Tripoli and his wife Hodierna of Jerusalem. He inherited the County of Tripoli after his father death in 1152. His mother acted as regent until he reached majority. He grew up in the crusader states surrounded by Muslim neighbors and Latin rivals. His early years were marked by efforts to secure his borders and to maintain the tribute owed to neighboring Muslim rulers.

*Political Alliances and Conflicts*
Raymond III became a key player in the politics of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. He supported Baldwin IV during his reign and fought alongside him at the Battle of Montgisard in 1177. He later opposed the rise of Guy of Lusignan and backed the claim of Isabella I to the throne. His diplomatic skills led him to negotiate truces with Saladin and to arrange marriages that strengthened ties between Tripoli and Jerusalem. However his relationship with the royal court soured after he was accused of conspiring against the king and he withdrew his support during the succession crisis of 1186. He refused to swear fealty to Guy and instead held Tripoli as an independent principality.

*Later Years and Death*
After the disastrous defeat at Hattin in 1186 Raymond III retreated to Tripoli where he organized the defense of the city against Saladin forces. He died in 1187 shortly after the fall of Jerusalem leaving his son Raymond IV to inherit a much reduced county. His legacy is remembered as that of a pragmatic lord who balanced warfare diplomacy and patronage in a turbulent era. Modern historians view him as a figure who tried to preserve crusader holdings through negotiation rather than endless war.
